input_facts.text:
On September 28, 2022 the BOE announces temporary, targeted purchases of long-dated UK government bonds to restore market functioning, with HM Treasury indemnification.
Auctions are planned from September 28 through October 14; purchases will be unwound once risks to market functioning have subsided. Scale is described as whatever is necessary for that objective.
The annual 80-billion-pound stock-reduction target remains unchanged, while the start of gilt sales is postponed to October 31. The MPC will assess developments at its next meeting and can change rates as needed for its inflation remit.

adjudication_excerpt.text: Temporary financial-stability purchases and a postponed sales start do not by themselves announce a policy-rate cut or abandon the annual stock-reduction target. The open scale statement is constrained by purpose and the stated auction window, not perpetual buying. October 14 is the planned end of purchase auctions, not a promised date by which every holding is sold. The release supplies plans, not proof of subsequent execution, solved dysfunction or returns.

question_en: Explain how the purchase operation, sales timetable, annual stock target and interest-rate decision process relate, including the scope and timing of the announced commitments.
